## Sachem Capital Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results


November 16, 2026


[Download (opens in new window) PDF 238 KB](https://s203.q4cdn.com/724831329/files/doc_news/Sachem-Capital-Reports-Third-Quarter-2026-Results-2026.pdf)


**– Provides Update on Pending Asset Contribution Transaction with Industrial Realty Group (IRG) –**


BRANFORD, Conn., Nov. 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Sachem Capital Corp. (NYSE American: SACH) (“Sachem” or the “Company”), a real estate lender specializing in originating, underwriting, funding, servicing, and managing a portfolio of loans secured by first mortgages on real property, today announced its financial results for the quarter and nine months ended September 30, 2026 and provided an update on the pending asset contribution transaction (the “Transaction”) with Industrial Realty Group (“IRG”).


John Villano, CPA, Sachem’s Chief Executive Officer, commented, “During the third quarter, we continued to make meaningful progress repositioning our loan portfolio, substantially reducing non-accrual loans since year-end. We also ended the quarter with a solid cash position. Our announced transaction with IRG, which would combine Sachem with a scaled portfolio of industrial real estate, represents a compelling opportunity for our shareholders. We are working diligently toward completion, including preparing pro forma financial statements and proxy materials. While the transaction remains subject to shareholder approval and other customary closing conditions, we remain focused on bringing it to a close, as we believe it can create significant long-term value for our shareholders.”


***Contribution Agreement with Industrial Realty Group Global, LLC***


As previously announced, the Company and IRG, a private real estate development and investment firm specializing in the acquisition, development and management of commercial and industrial real estate throughout the United States, entered into a definitive contribution agreement on May 17, 2026, under which IRG will contribute 98 industrial assets (“the Contribution Portfolio”) from its 200-asset portfolio owned by IRG and/or its partners to Sachem, and once completed, the combined company will operate as IRG Realty Trust, Inc. ("IRGT").


IRG will contribute the Contribution Portfolio to a newly formed Sachem operating partnership in exchange for operating partnership units and Class B common stock, based on a deemed value of $2.00 per Sachem common share. Following the closing, IRG is expected to hold approximately 94.1% of the operating partnership units, with Sachem shareholders retaining approximately 5.9%. At closing, Sachem expects to effect a 20-to-1 reverse stock split and change its name to IRG Realty Trust, Inc. The transaction was unanimously approved by Sachem’s Board of Directors and remains subject to shareholder approval and other closing conditions.


Upon closing, IRGT is expected to own 98 industrial properties having a gross real estate asset value of $2.9 billion, plus Sachem's approximately $467 million of total assets in direct and indirect mortgage loans, investments in developmental and owned real estate, and other assets. IRGT is expected to have an implied enterprise value of approximately $3.4 billion, positioning IRGT as a top‑10 publicly listed industrial REIT based on enterprise value. IRGT will focus on mission‑critical industrial infrastructure supporting manufacturing and distribution users. The assets not being contributed will continue to be owned and operated by IRG's existing private business, Industrial Realty Group, LLC.


***Industrial Realty Group Transaction and Portfolio Update***


- Approximately 3.0 million square feet of new and renewal leases were signed, representing $13.5 million of Annual Base Rent (“ABR”) during the third quarter 2026.
- Included in the above, 1.0 million square feet of new leases were signed representing $6.3 million of ABR.
- The Company and IRG continue to work toward completing the Transaction, which is currently expected to close in the first quarter of 2027, subject to the satisfaction of customary closing conditions, including the approval of the Company’s shareholders. The Company will provide additional updates during the fourth quarter as the Transaction progresses.


For additional information on the Contribution Agreement and the Transaction, see the Company's Current Report on Form 8-K filed with the SEC on May 18, 2026, and the Company's Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.


***Portfolio and Asset Management Updates***


**Coconut Grove, Florida** . Following the sale of one residence during the third quarter, two residences remain as collateral for the related-party loans. One is being marketed for sale and the other is nearing completion of outdoor amenities and will be listed for sale in the fourth quarter. Subject to market conditions, we expect both properties to sell in the first half of 2027.


**Vela Bay - Naples, Florida** . Construction activity on the south building has commenced, including ground improvement work and presale activities. Subject to market conditions, we expect to sell the three completed north building residences in the first half of 2027. Our current estimate of remaining project expenditures is approximately $18.0 million through the fourth quarter of 2028. These estimates are subject to construction progress, costs, market conditions and sales timing; anticipated sales are not assured. Urbane Capital, our in-house asset management and development platform, continues to oversee the development and monetization of the project.


***Loan Portfolio***


- During the third quarter, we originated 11 loans and disbursed $36.8 million (including modifications and draws) while 12 loans, totaling $52.3 million, were repaid.
- Gross principal amount of loans held for investment was $320.0 million across 98 loans at September 30, 2026, compared to $377.4 million across 115 loans at December 31, 2025.
- Weighted average contractual interest rate, including default interest, was 11.43%, compared to 13.10% at December 31, 2025.
- Loans on non-accrual status had an outstanding principal balance of $84.6 million, compared to $117.6 million at December 31, 2025.
- No borrower exceeded 10% of the outstanding mortgage loan portfolio at September 30, 2026, compared to one borrower representing 13.3% of the loan portfolio at December 31, 2025.


***Sachem’s Results of Operations for the Quarter Ended September 30, 2026***


Net interest income was $1.1 million compared to $2.7 million in the third quarter of 2025. The year-over-year change was primarily due to a $1.7 million reduction in interest income from loans as average performing loan balances were lower by $36.3 million and the effective yield on performing loans declined. As the Company continued to reduce its limited liability company investments, interest income from limited liability company investments decreased $0.4 million while interest expense decreased $0.5 million due to lower average borrowings. Utilizing the average performing loans held for investment balance for the quarter of $231.8 million, the effective yield on performing loans was 11.5%. Comparatively, using the average performing loans held for investment balance for the third quarter of 2025 of $268.1 million, the effective yield on performing loans was 12.4%.


The Company’s net interest margin was 1.4% for the third quarter, compared to 2.9% for the third quarter 2025. Net interest margin represents net interest income, calculated as annualized interest income less annualized interest expense, expressed as a percentage of average loans held for investment outstanding for the applicable period. The change in net interest margin reflects both structural and cyclical factors. Structurally, refinancing activity during 2025 increased the weighted average cost of capital. Cyclically, lower average earning assets reduced interest-earning balances.


Provision for credit losses related to loans held for investment was $0.5 million, compared with $0.8 million in the third quarter of 2025. The decrease was primarily due to stabilization in collateral valuations for loans previously reserved and fewer nonperforming loans.


Total other income was $1.8 million compared to $4.1 million in the same quarter last year, primarily due to decline in fee income on loans due to lower new loan origination volume, the absence of $1.4 million of gains on equity securities recorded in the same quarter last year, and decrease in rental income as a result of the sale of developmental real estate in December 2025.


Total operating costs and expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were $4.6 million compared to $5.0 million in the same quarter last year. The decrease was primarily related to lower compensation and employee benefits and general and administrative expenses, partially offset by transaction expenses, as discussed further below.


- Compensation and employee benefits were $1.9 million, compared to $2.3 million in the same quarter last year, reflecting nonrecurring awards in the same quarter last year.
- General and administrative expenses were $1.4 million, versus $1.7 million from the same quarter last year, primarily due to lower costs associated with our investments in developmental real estate.
- Transaction expenses were $0.8 million versus none in the same quarter last year, all of which were incurred in connection with the Transaction. We expect to incur additional material costs prior to the closing of the Transaction.
- There were no non-cash impairment losses on real estate in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $0.2 million in the same quarter last year, which related to specific property-level valuation adjustments following updated market data and liquidation timelines.
- Gain on sale of investments in developmental real estate, real estate owned and property and equipment, net was $0.1 million, compared to a net loss of $0.3 million in the same quarter last year, reflecting gains realized on the disposition of select real estate assets and developmental projects during the period.


Net loss attributable to common shareholders for the third quarter of 2026 was $3.2 million, or $0.07 per common share, compared to net loss attributable to common shareholders of $0.1 million, or $0.00 per common share for the third quarter of 2025. The current-quarter loss was significantly affected by $0.8 million of transaction expenses associated with the Transaction.


***Balance Sheet***


At quarter end, total assets were $467.4 million compared to $460.0 million as of December 31, 2025, primarily reflecting a $30.5 million increase in cash and a $40.9 million increase in investments in developmental real estate, partially offset by a $57.2 million decrease in loans held for investment, net. The changes in developmental real estate and loans were primarily driven by the Naples, Florida loan restructuring in the first quarter of 2026. Total liabilities were $312.2 million compared to $285.1 million as of December 31, 2025, primarily due to a $12.0 million increase in borrowings under the revolving credit facility and a $10.4 million increase in senior secured notes payable.


Total indebtedness at quarter end was $301.3 million. This includes $172.4 million of unsecured notes payable (net of $0.9 million of deferred financing costs), $97.0 million of senior secured notes payable (net of $3.0 million of deferred financing costs), $31.0 million outstanding on a $50.0 million revolving credit facility and $0.9 million of outstanding principal on a loan secured by a mortgage on the Company’s office building. Approximately $51.8 million of unsecured notes payable are due and payable on December 30, 2026.


Total shareholders’ equity as of September 30, 2026, was $155.2 million compared to $174.9 million as of December 31, 2025, primarily reflecting the nine-month net loss of $13.6 million and $6.7 million of dividends paid.


***Book value per common share***


Book value per common share as of September 30, 2026, was $2.03, as compared to $2.46 as of December 31, 2025. This change was primarily due to cash dividends declared and paid for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 on issued and outstanding common shares and shares of Series A Preferred Stock totaling an aggregate of $6.7 million, or $0.14 per common share, and net loss for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 of $13.6 million, or $0.28 per common share.


The nine month period's net loss impacting the book value per common share was materially driven by the non-cash discounted cash flow fair value adjustment on loan restructuring recorded in provision for credit losses related to loans held for investment of $3.9 million, or $0.08 per common share, and expenses related to the Transaction of $4.9 million, or $0.10 per common share. The aggregate impact of these events is $8.8 million, or $0.18 per common share of book value, decline from year end.


***Dividends***


The Company currently operates and qualifies as a Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT) for federal income tax purposes and intends to continue to qualify and operate as a REIT. Under federal income tax rules, a REIT is required to distribute a minimum of 90% of taxable income each year to its shareholders, and the Company intends to comply with this requirement for the current year.


On September 30, 2026, the Company paid a dividend of $0.484375 per share to the holders of its Series A Preferred Stock and $0.01 per share to its common shareholders of record on September 15, 2026.


**About Sachem Capital Corp**


Sachem is a mortgage REIT that specializes in originating, underwriting, funding, servicing, and managing a portfolio of loans secured by first mortgages on real property. It offers short-term (i.e., one to three years), secured, nonbanking loans to real estate investors to fund their acquisition, renovation, development, rehabilitation, or improvement of properties. The Company’s primary underwriting criteria is a conservative loan to value ratio. The properties securing the loans are generally classified as residential or commercial real estate and, typically, are held for resale or investment. Loans are secured by mortgage liens on real estate and often are personally guaranteed by the principal(s) of the borrower. The Company also makes opportunistic real estate purchases apart from its lending activities.
